Working with the school

1 tool

School emails and meeting checklist

Three emails ready to copy and send from your phone, and what to bring, ask, and do at the meeting.

WebPrintable PDF
Subject: Request to meet about [child's name] Hi [Name], I'm reaching out because [child's name] has been dealing with [hurtful messages / posts / a group chat] involving other students since [date]. I've saved copies of what's been happening. I'd like to meet so we can work together to make sure [he / she / they] feels safe at school. I'm available [days and times]. Please let me know what works for you. Thank you, [Your name] [Phone number]
Subject: Following up on our meeting about [child's name] Hi [Name], Thank you for meeting with me today. I want to make sure I understood our plan: - [What the school will do] - [Who is handling it] - [How [child's name] will be kept safe in the meantime] - [When we'll talk next] Please let me know if I missed anything. I appreciate your help. Thank you, [Your name]
Subject: Checking in on [child's name] Hi [Name], I wanted to check in on the plan we talked about on [date]. [Since then, things have gotten better / the messages have continued / I haven't heard an update.] Could you let me know where things stand, and when we might talk next? Thank you, [Your name]

At the meeting

  • Bring your evidence log and printed screenshots
  • Ask who will look into it and how they’ll keep your child safe in the meantime
  • Ask them not to put the kids in a room together to “work it out”
  • Agree on a date for your next conversation
  • Send the follow-up email the same day
See the emails and checklist

Still no change? Write to the principal, then the superintendent, and attach your evidence log and these emails. If the bullying is about race, national origin, sex, disability, or religion, say so in writing.
